target_turkana_adults.population: Adults aged at least 18 with recorded sex F or M in the selected Turkana 2018-2019 study-protocol target context; demographic and lifestyle mixture unspecified
target_turkana_adults.measurement: Recorded study-protocol total and HDL cholesterol represented in canonical mmol/L; no assay or fasting equivalence asserted

assumptions.description: Use the released whole-cohort interface: observed is None, every context contains 5000 independent synthetic draws, ordered task columns and units are unchanged, and recorded category codes are literal strings. The target descriptor and source population/measurement strings are copied mechanically. These are synthetic records, not new clinical evidence.

Treat each source subgroup as a proxy distribution conditional on its reported adult/health/complete-lipid selection. Unreported eligibility variables and variable-specific missingness are not reconstructed. A single synthetic source table uses the available subgroup summaries jointly despite differing Table 1/Table 2 counts. This is a construction assumption, not a claim of reconstructing the original participants.

For explicitly proposed raw descriptive proxies, interpret the published subgroup geometric means and low-HDL percentages as anchors of an equal-weight probability distribution. Published source weights are not reported. Comparisons of exp(mean(log(x))) and 100*mean(HDL<c) are assumption-defined descriptive comparisons, not verified replications of the source estimators; c retains the strict reported sex-specific threshold.

Within each source profile BMI, TC and HDL have lognormal marginal distributions. BMI log SD is 0.18 and TC log SD is 0.25, independently assumed rather than inferred from confidence intervals. HDL marginal log SD is the finite equation [log(c)-log(G)]/Phi_inverse(p), with p=reported low-HDL percentage/100 and G=reported HDL geometric mean. Positive finite solutions are required; no fallback, optimizer or sample-based adjustment is used. This HDL dispersion is family-dependent and is not a reported individual or conditional residual SD.

The joint law is a Gaussian factor construction with independent latent A,B,H,T. Age is increasing in A; BMI score is 0.18*A+sqrt(1-0.18^2)*B; HDL score is 0.06*A-0.18*B+sqrt(1-0.06^2-0.18^2)*H; TC score is 0.22*A+0.30*B+0.35*H+sqrt(1-0.22^2-0.30^2-0.35^2)*T. These chosen weak age, adiposity and shared-lipid dependencies are scientific assumptions, not estimates from pooled Table 3. They permit dependence after age/BMI adjustment. No independence or zero effect is inferred from absent evidence.

All contexts use age=18-22*log(Phi(-A)), an adult shifted-exponential age distribution with mean excess age 22 years, selected as a broad simple age scenario with no upper cutoff. It is not fitted to reported age medians or quartiles. Those context-only summaries are not executable calibration targets.

Each source context selects its own profile with weight one and uses the source-internal male-to-M/female-to-F convention. The target is an equal mixture of six external source summary profiles; these are unlabelled mathematical profiles, not Turkana lifestyle/site categories or a representativeness claim. Target weights do not use source sample sizes, precisions, target rows or outcomes. The target is a declared reference scenario because its actual composition is unknown.

Target F/M labels are assigned independently with probability F=0.5, independently of profile, age and clinical factors. Source labels use F probability zero for men and one for women. Target label exchangeability is an explicit assumption that avoids claiming an unverified biological legend; it imposes no population sex association in the target scenario and is not empirical evidence for a null sex effect.

Source marginals include each source assay/fasting regime. The target reuses their log locations and profile-specific dispersions as a provisional transport scenario, with extra mean-zero log measurement/transport noise SD 0.06 for TC and 0.09 for HDL and correlation 0.25. Source extra-noise SDs are zero because their measured distributions already supply the anchors. Zero log offsets in all contexts are a chosen central scenario, not verified absence of assay bias. The target extra variability is not a calibrated assay-error estimate and cannot correct unknown systematic shifts.

TC and HDL are generated as positive measured analytes with joint latent dependence, without enforcing TC>=HDL or filtering rows. The model can produce HDL above TC. Non-HDL geometric means are retained evidence but are not used to invent a subtraction-of-geometric-means constraint or an unavailable derived diagnostic.

All source profiles come from the same admitted Greiner paper and overlapping cohort analyses; no independent-study replication or precision pooling is claimed. Rounded/collapsed CIs remain estimator uncertainty; the anomalous Malawi urban women HDL CI is not used. Table-specific counts remain provenance, not row requirements, weights or dispersion estimators. Table 3 scales and adjustment sets remain unresolved and no coefficient enters this model.

The frozen construction represents one conditional-on-assumptions scenario. Random draws express individual variation only. Target composition, distribution families, dependence, source selection, biological sex-code mapping and CardioChek Plus venous-EDTA/unknown-fasting transport are structurally uncertain and are not assigned probability distributions. Source agreement would not validate target slopes, residual correlation, causal effects or clinical utility.

active_context.derivation: Mechanically set to the supplied target context ID. Only this top-level field changes between source/target executions.

contexts.derivation: Population, n_rows and measurement are copied from released descriptors. Source weights are one-hot; target weights are six equal unnormalised ones, normalised deterministically inside generate. Source F probabilities encode the declared strata; target F probability is a label-exchangeable scenario. Measurement arrays are ordered TC,HDL, with fixed assumed target excess noise and zero central offsets.

profile_order.derivation: Supplied source-template order; indices bind profile_weights to source_anchors without introducing target categories.

source_anchors.derivation: Exact published point estimates for BMI, TC and HDL geometric means and strict low-HDL prevalence/threshold are copied. In generate, before any random draw, mu_X=log(G_X), p=low_hdl_percent/100 and sigma_H=[log(c)-log(G_H)]/ndtri(p). All six positive finite sigmas are derived once; no empirical CI, group n or generated data enters. Threshold values are 1.03 mmol/L for source men and 1.29 mmol/L for source women. No claim of known original weights or exact source estimator reconstruction.

age_settings.derivation: Fixed minimum 18 from the task and chosen mean excess 22 years. For standard normal A, Phi(-A) is uniform so -log(Phi(-A)) is unit exponential; scipy.special.log_ndtr evaluates the log CDF stably. No reported quantile is fitted.

marginal_settings.derivation: Fixed assumed marginal log SDs: BMI 0.18 and TC 0.25. HDL marginal dispersion is separately derived from source_anchors under A03.

factor_settings.derivation: Fixed factor loadings chosen for a weak age relation, adiposity/lipid relation and shared lipid residual. Remaining loadings are finite square roots of one minus each row sum of squared specified loadings, derived before random draws to give unit-normal scores. Their values are not Table 3 coefficients or raw-scale regression slopes. Profiles share this structure; different marginal dispersions and mixture composition change raw-scale associations.

measurement_settings.derivation: Fixed assumed excess log-error correlation r=0.25. With independent standard normals E1,E2, TC log error=s_TC*E1 and HDL log error=s_H*(r*E1+sqrt(1-r^2)*E2). Context log offsets are added on their respective measured-analyte scales. Extra source noise has zero variance; target noise is a declared unvalidated transport scenario.

output_columns.derivation: Copied ordered task columns: id, age, sex, bmi, total_cholesterol, hdl_cholesterol. Age years; BMI kg/m^2; lipids mmol/L.
